_note: v2 hook overrides for la Tour de l'Horloge (B03_horloge): only where the painted scene differs from the source hook.

fr_vendredi_noun.hook: "VAN-DRUH-DEE" ("vahn-druh-DEE"): the fishmonger pushes his little blue fish cart, a tiny VAN of fish: fish day, FRIDAY.
fr_vendredi_noun.why: The painting shows a small blue handcart of fish rather than a motor van.

fr_fin_noun.hook: "FAN" ("FAN"): the girl gives her FAN one last flourish. That's THE END of the show.
fr_fin_noun.why: The painted fan is open, not being snapped shut.

fr_soir_noun.hook: A SWAN ("SWAHR") glides on the little fountain pond as the day draws to a close: it is EVENING.
fr_soir_noun.why: The repainted square shows the swan on a fountain pond, with no street lamp.

fr_matin_noun.hook: "MAT-TAN" ("ma-TAN"): a man does sunrise yoga on his MAT as the sun comes up behind him: MORNING.
fr_matin_noun.why: The repainted square has no rooster.

fr_demain_adv.hook: "DUH-MAN" ("duh-MAN"): THE MAN, already in his pyjamas and nightcap, yawns on his packed suitcase holding up his alarm clock: he leaves TOMORROW morning.
fr_demain_adv.why: RECS p15: the man is now painted (pyjamas, packed case, alarm clock) so THE MAN + tomorrow are both visible.

fr_reprise_noun.hook: "RE-PRIZE" ("ruh-PREEZ"): a girl holds her trophy up high. She won the PRIZE AGAIN, a REPEAT.
fr_reprise_noun.why: The music room shows one trophy.

fr_initiation_noun.hook: "ee-nee-sya-SYON": "INITIATE me!" A girl kneels holding up her very first paintbrush, ready for her first painting lesson: her INITIATION.
fr_initiation_noun.why: wooden sword replaced with a paintbrush (no weapons)

fr_introduction_noun.hook: "an-tro-duk-SYON": microphone in hand, she waves hello for the INTRODUCTION: "Let me introduce myself."
fr_introduction_noun.why: The terrace shows her waving rather than shaking hands.

fr_rendez_vous_noun.hook: A smart little boy with a bouquet checks his pocket watch: his RENDEZVOUS is late! English borrowed the same word.

fr_jour_noun.hook: "ZHOOR", like SURE: the doorman holds up a smiling golden sun. "SURE is a lovely DAY!" The sun means DAY.
fr_jour_noun.why: hook no longer relies on the French word bonjour

fr_hebdomadaire_adj.hook: "EBB-DOME-A-DARE" ("eb-doh-ma-DAIR"): the paperboy brings the WEEKLY magazine, the same day every seven days.

fr_minute_noun.hook: "MEAN NUT!" ("mee-NOOT"): a grumpy little boy on a stool hugs his big NUT and frowns: he won't share it for even one MINUTE.
fr_minute_noun.why: MEAN NUT gives the sound; a boy replaces the squirrel on a stool (the squirrel was not the sound-alike).

fr_nuit_noun.hook: A sleepy GNU, "GNU-EE" ("NWEE"), lies curled up asleep on the floor, a white nightcap hung on its horn and a crescent-moon lantern glowing beside it: bedtime, it is NIGHT.
fr_nuit_noun.why: "GNU-EE" gives the sound "NWEE"; the sleeping gnu, nightcap and moon lantern all say NIGHT. A natural four-legged gnu, nothing worn.

fr_journee_noun.hook: "JOURNEY" ("zhoor-NAY"): a traveller with a suitcase and walking stick sets off through the archway on a JOURNEY that will take the whole DAY.
fr_journee_noun.why: JOURNEY gives the sound "zhoor-NAY"; a journey that lasts all day is a JOURNÉE (a whole day).

fr_maintenant_adv.hook: "man-tuh-NAHN": at the rocket launch a MAN counts down from TEN on his fingers and NAN slams the button: NOW! maintenant = now.

fr_toujours_adv.hook: "too-ZHOOR": the eager schoolboy is TOO SURE of himself: his hand is ALWAYS up first, and it's STILL up when the bell rings. toujours = always, still.

fr_aujourd_hui_adv.hook: "oh-zhoor-DWEE": the librarian stamps the date in a library book with a little SUN stamp: "OH, YOUR DUE-EE date is TODAY!" aujourd'hui = today.

fr_periode_noun.hook: Like English PERIOD (pay-RYOD) — the trap is the article: LA période. The accordion player squeezes out one long PERIOD of music.

fr_bientot_adv.hook: "BEE-AN-TOE" ("byan-TOH"): a BEE hovers over the closed tulip bud on the shelf, waiting: it will open SOON. bientôt = soon.

fr_souvent_adv.hook: "SOO-VAN" ("soo-VAHN"): the boy shows off his SOUVENIR VAN, plastered with travel stickers: it goes on trips OFTEN. souvent = often.

fr_hier_adv.hook: "EE-AIR" ("YEHR"): the old schoolmaster holds his brass EAR trumpet to the drooping rose: it was fresh YESTERDAY. hier = yesterday.

fr_lors_adv.hook: "LOR(D)" ("LOR"): a boy dressed as a little LORD mayor, robe and gold chain, for the school play, AT THE TIME OF the show. lors de = at the time of, during.

fr_puis_adv.hook: "PWEE!" ("PWEE"): the girl tips one domino, PWEE! THEN the next falls, THEN the next. puis = then, next.

fr_quelquefois_adv.hook: "SHELL-KUH-FWAH" ("kehl-kuh-FWAH"): the girl opens a big SHELL and, NOW AND THEN, there's a pearl inside. quelquefois = sometimes, now and then.

fr_tot_adv.hook: "TOE" ("TOH"): an alarm clock is tied to the sleepy boy's big TOE, so he'll wake up EARLY. tôt = early.

fr_autrefois_adv.hook: "AUTO-FWAH" ("oh-truh-FWAH"): the boy holds an old brass AUTO, a toy car from IN THE OLD DAYS. autrefois = in the past, formerly.

fr_actuellement_adv.hook: "ACTUAL-MAN" ("ahk-tweh-luh-MAHN"): the red lamp glows on the old radio: the children are on air RIGHT NOW. actuellement = currently (false friend: NOT 'actually', which is en fait).

fr_parfois_adv.hook: "PAR-FWAH" ("pahr-FWAH"): the boy putts the golf ball at the little hole: he makes PAR... SOMETIMES. parfois = sometimes.

fr_malheureusement_adv.hook: "MAL-A-ROSE-MAN" ("mah-leuh-reuh-zuh-MAHN"): the poor little man has knocked over the rose pot, soil everywhere. UNFORTUNATELY! malheureusement = unfortunately.
